issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition proceeding is void when the land and all interests in it already belong to the State and nothing remains for the State to acquire.
material_facts: The former landholder had a possessory interest but no ownership interest in the land.
The State took possession of the land, resumed it, and recorded it as State land before the later acquisition proceeding began.
No right, title, interest, or possession remained with the former landholder or his successors when the later proceeding was initiated.
The State subsequently initiated a fresh acquisition proceeding and an award was made, although the land had already become State land.
issues.conclusion: The fresh acquisition proceeding and the award made under it were nullities and ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Jammu and Kashmir State Land Acquisition Act, 1934, does not provide for acquisition of an interest that already belongs to the Government; the Act applies only to interests in land that do not already belong to the Government. The Court relied on Government of Bombay v. Esufali Salebhai, Mohammad Wajeeh Mirza v. Secretary of State for India in Council, The Deputy Collector, Calicut Division v. Aiyavu Pillay, and The Collector of Bombay v. Nusserwanji Rattanji Mistri. It distinguished Secy. of State v. Tayasaheb Yeshwantrao Holkar and Marriot v. Hamoton because those cases involved payment under an award and, in the relevant circumstances, possession held by the other party; here, neither title nor possession remained outside the State. Whether the proceeding arose through fraud, mistake, negligence, or otherwise did not alter its invalidity.

predicates.state_land_acquisition_proceeding: A proceeding was initiated to acquire land under a land acquisition process.
predicates.land_already_owned_and_possessed_by_stat: The State had already resumed the land and held both ownership and possession before the later proceeding began.
predicates.no_private_interest_remaining: No private right, title, interest, or possession in the land remained when the later proceeding began.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition proceeding concerns land already owned and possessed by the State with no private interest remaining, the proceeding and its resulting award are void.

issues.legal_issue: A prior appeal confined to determining compensation does not bar a later suit challenging the acquisition proceeding as a nullity when the nullity issue was outside the appeal's scope and the claimant did not change position in reliance on the proceeding.
material_facts: An earlier appeal under the land acquisition process concerned the amount of compensation.

The challenge that the acquisition proceeding was a nullity was raised in an application and a review in connection with that appeal, but determining the proceeding's validity was outside the appeal's scope.
The claimant had already lost possession of the land before the acquisition proceeding and sought compensation; the proceeding did not cause him to change his position.
issues.conclusion: The prior proceedings did not operate as res judicata, and estoppel did not prevent the later suit challenging the acquisition proceeding and award.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal under the land acquisition process that is limited to determining compensation does not confer jurisdiction to declare the entire acquisition proceeding a nullity. Statements on an issue outside that appeal's scope cannot operate as res judicata. Estoppel does not arise where the person against whom it is asserted was not made to change position by the proceeding. The Court also noted that the applications under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure and for review were beyond the scope of the compensation appeal.

rule.if: suit_challenging_prior_acquisition_order and prior_appeal_limited_to_compensation and nullity_issue_outside_prior_scope and claimant_position_unchanged

predicates.suit_challenging_prior_acquisition_order: A suit was brought to challenge an acquisition proceeding or award previously addressed in another proceeding.
predicates.prior_appeal_limited_to_compensation: The earlier appeal was confined to determining the compensation payable.
predicates.nullity_issue_outside_prior_scope: The validity of the acquisition proceeding as a whole was outside the matters the earlier appeal could decide.
predicates.claimant_position_unchanged: The claimant did not change position because of the acquisition proceeding and had already lost possession of the land.

issues.definition: When a nullity suit follows a compensation-only appeal that could not decide the validity of the acquisition, and the claimant did not change position because of the proceeding, the prior orders do not bar the suit.
